solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Keenness shown in going through maze alone

indicators.note: the answer is on show inside the words that follow, running across the gap between them

explanation.surface: Someone shows real eagerness by tackling a maze without help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going through' is a link joining the definition to the text the letters sit in: maZE ALone.
explanation.definitionFit: Keenness and fervour for a cause are synonyms, both naming eager enthusiasm.

clue.text: Joins academic institution to education newspaper?

parts.note: uni is the short form of university
the TES is the Times Educational Supplement, a British weekly for teachers

explanation.surface: A university teams up with a teachers' paper, perhaps in a sponsorship deal.
explanation.walkthrough: The TES is a British trade paper for schoolteachers.
explanation.definitionFit: To join things and to bring them together as one are synonyms, both verbs in the third person.

clue.text: Sponsored individual, one following surgeon into leading position

indicators.note: the surgeon and the one are placed inside the word for leading position

parts.note: gold is first place, the top medal

indicators.note: following puts the one after the surgeon, so the clue's order is swapped

parts.note: DCh is the abbreviation for Doctor of Surgery (Chirurgiae)
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A sponsored person is placed in a top post after a surgeon.
explanation.walkthrough: DCh, Doctor of Surgery, is a less familiar medical degree abbreviation; 'leading position' is first place, the gold medal.
explanation.definitionFit: A child whose baptismal sponsors are godparents is sponsored in that religious sense.

clue.text: Racial rioting in the college

indicators.note: rioting means running wild, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Riots at a college are said to have racial motives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rioting' looks like part of the picture but is the anagram signal for the two small words before 'college'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethnic and racial both describe groups sharing ancestry or culture, adjectives in the same sense.

clue.text: Joint around US city's sufficing for poet

indicators.note: the joint surrounds the city and its possessive letter

parts.note: a tenon is the projecting part of a woodworking joint
NY is New York, with the S from the possessive

explanation.surface: A carpentry joint built round an American city stands in for a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sufficing for' is a link meaning 'will do as', joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred, Lord Tennyson was the Victorian Poet Laureate, an example of a poet.

clue.text: Bloke seizing trophy upset many a hired worker

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold of, so the bloke surrounds the trophy

parts.note: Joe is a generic name for an ordinary man
an urn is a classic trophy shape, as in cricket's Ashes urn

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of the following word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man grabs a cup, annoying many people who had hired help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like the bloke's mood but signals rearranging 'many'; 'a' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A journeyman is a qualified tradesman employed by a master, so a worker for hire.

clue.text: Final situation when we all learn to fly?

definitions.meaning: the point beyond which nothing more can be done, the finish

definitions.text: when we all learn to fly?
definitions.meaning: a playful image: if everyone could fly, roads would no longer be needed and would come to their finish

explanation.surface: A dreamy question about the ultimate future when everyone takes to the air.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is whimsical: flight would make the highway obsolete, ending the era of roads.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means the point where something can go no further, a last stage.

clue.text: Extended sentence? Prisoners not initially angry

parts.note: time is a prison sentence, as in doing time
cons is short for convicts

indicators.note: says the first letter of the angry word is dropped

parts.note: fuming means furious

explanation.surface: Convicts are furious about a long prison term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extended sentence?' reads as one idea, but 'Extended' alone is the definition and 'sentence' is TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that eats up a lot of hours is lengthy or drawn out, so extended.

clue.text: Marauders rage wrecking this plantation crop

indicators.note: wrecking means smashing up, so these letters are broken apart and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Raiders on the rampage trash a plantation's harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of MARAUDERS RAGE is the crop; 'this' points to the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Demerara sugar is a light brown cane sugar from Guyana, an example of a plantation product.

clue.text: Fine backsliding corporation storing chlorine

indicators.note: sliding back, so the whole assembled piece reads in the opposite direction
storing means holding within, so the belly word wraps round the chemical symbol

parts.note: corporation is an old jocular word for a pot belly, a tum
Cl is the chemical symbol for chlorine

explanation.surface: A company that has gone back on promises is fined for keeping a toxic gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' meaning a paunch is an old jocular sense and a crossword favourite; 'Fine' is the verb, to penalise.
explanation.definitionFit: To mulct is to extract money by a fine or penalty, a formal verb sense.

clue.text: Fake getting round sister with booze? Mysterious stuff

indicators.note: getting round means surrounding, so the fake word encloses the sister

parts.note: cod as an adjective means sham or mock
a nun is a religious sister
rum is a spirit, a kind of booze

explanation.surface: A con involving a nun and a bottle of drink is a puzzling business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fake' as cod is a British informal adjective, as in a cod accent.
explanation.definitionFit: A conundrum is a riddle or baffling problem, matter that puzzles and mystifies.

clue.text: Cut-down strongbox with notes about church bishops?

indicators.note: cut down means shortened, so the box word loses its last letter

parts.note: a chest is a strong box for valuables

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the notes word wraps round the church

parts.note: notes as a verb means observes, spies
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A shortened strongbox is found with jottings about church leaders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' looks like a noun but is the verb, giving SPIES, which surrounds CE. The question mark flags bishops as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Bishops are among the pieces on a chessboard, so the definition is an example of the plural.

clue.text: Sex and nature out of joint — involving love is irrelevant

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the shuffled letters surround the love
out of joint means dislocated, so the letters are shifted out of place

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A claim that sex and nature are mismatched, and love has no bearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of joint' scrambles the first two words to EXTRANEUS, and the O of love goes in near the end; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Extraneous matter is beside the point, unrelated to the subject, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Frontless dress gets attention

indicators.note: without its front, so the opening letter of the dress word is removed

parts.note: wear as a noun means clothing, as in evening wear

explanation.surface: A daringly open-fronted gown draws everyone's eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: To lend an ear is to listen, so ear means heed or attention.

clue.text: Observed before decoration?

definitions.meaning: a cake before decoration has not been iced

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the answer into NOT ICED, a cake before its icing.
explanation.definitionFit: Noticed and observed are synonyms, both past tense verbs for seeing something.

clue.text: Conservative Right beset by difficult situations, provoking laughs

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so the right abbreviation goes inside the word for difficult situations

parts.note: being in a hole is being in trouble, so holes are tight spots

explanation.surface: Tory right-wingers in trouble cause people to laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provoking' is a link: the clue's events lead to the laughs.
explanation.definitionFit: To chortle is to laugh gleefully, a word coined by Lewis Carroll; both are verbs.

clue.text: Molecule in compound beginning to mutate no more

indicators.note: takes only the opening letter of the next word
compound as a verb means mix together, so these letters are combined anew

explanation.surface: A chemist's molecule within a compound will stop changing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound' looks like the chemistry noun but is the anagram signal for M plus NO MORE.
explanation.definitionFit: A monomer is a small molecule that can link with others to form a polymer, a type of molecule.

clue.text: Vegetarian diet followed by male? On the contrary

indicators.note: reverses the stated order, so the male comes first and the diet follows it

parts.note: to diet is to eat less

explanation.surface: A meat-free regime is tried, with a man following it, or the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'followed by' would put the diet first, but 'On the contrary' flips that: M, then EAT LESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A vegetarian meal contains no flesh, so the two adjectives mean the same.

clue.text: Girl half incapacitated?

indicators.note: half signals keeping only the front portion of the synonym

parts.note: unable means lacking the capacity

explanation.walkthrough: The front half of UNABLE gives the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Una is a female first name, so an example of a girl.

clue.text: Chances going round hole in beach, finding various things

indicators.note: going round means surrounding, so the chances word encloses the rest

parts.note: odds are chances or probabilities

indicators.note: places the hole inside the beach

parts.note: sand stands for a beach
a den is a lair or hole

explanation.surface: Taking a gamble round a burrow on the shore uncovers assorted objects.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: the hole goes into the beach, making SANDEND, and that whole piece sits within the chances word.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds and ends is an idiom for miscellaneous leftover items, an assortment.

clue.text: Stepped up to collect money, making escape

indicators.note: to collect means to take in, so the turned word holds the money letter
in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: paced means walked with steps

explanation.surface: Someone came forward to pick up cash, then ran off with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns PACED into DECAP, which takes M in. 'making' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To decamp is to leave suddenly or secretly, to abscond, so a verb for escape.

clue.text: Party fronting wise measure

indicators.note: fronting means standing in front of, so the party word comes first

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
sage means wise

explanation.surface: A party sets the scene for a sensible amount.
explanation.definitionFit: A dosage is a measured quantity of medicine to be taken, a measure.

clue.text: Iodine on the teeth, surrounding one canine, showing no change

parts.note: I is the chemical symbol for iodine

indicators.note: the teeth word goes round the one and the canine

parts.note: dental means relating to the teeth
I is the Roman numeral one
C is the dental notation for a canine tooth

explanation.surface: An antiseptic dabbed on teeth, round a dog's tooth, makes no difference.
explanation.walkthrough: In dentists' tooth charts C labels the canine, a convention outside the usual abbreviation lists.
explanation.definitionFit: Things exactly alike, with no difference between them, are identical, an adjective sense.

clue.text: Squealed about lecturer's form of language

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the squealed word goes round the lecturer's letter

parts.note: to sing is ... for informing, so squealed means sang
L is an abbreviation for lecturer

explanation.surface: Someone squealed about a lecturer's way of talking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squealed' means informed on the police: criminals sing.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang is very informal vocabulary, a register or variety of speech.

clue.text: It's not for me, repeatedly dodging intervening period

indicators.note: dodging means avoiding, so the doubled letters are taken out

parts.note: the meantime is the interval between two events

indicators.note: repeatedly calls for the small word twice

parts.note: the clue's own two letters

explanation.surface: Someone says it is not their sort of thing, repeatedly avoiding the interval.
explanation.walkthrough: MEANTIME loses ME at its start and its end. 'It's not for me' looks like the definition, but 'me' is the letters to remove.
explanation.definitionFit: An anti is someone opposed, a person who is against rather than in favour.

clue.text: Student song: a mug and I used guitar in arrangement

indicators.note: in arrangement means the letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Students strum a guitar, cup in hand, for a rousing song.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of A MUG and I USED GUITAR gives the Latin title.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaudeamus Igitur, Latin for 'let us rejoice', is the traditional university anthem, an example of a student song.
